title: LIVE NOW: CPI DATA INFLATION REPORT OCT. 2026
speaker: Ricky Gutierrez

macro_themes.view: Headline CPI 3.7% vs 3.6% expected and core 2.6% vs 2.5%; a hotter print justifies the market selling off.
Energy, especially fuel oil (+15.3% m/m), is the biggest driver, tied to Middle East / Strait of Hormuz escalation and Russia sanctions.
Irrational valuations are only supported in irrational times; the most speculative stocks crash hardest when markets sell off.

calls.condition: Wants it to sell off toward 900 to buy; notes support could break if the selloff continues after the open.
calls.reason: Low P/E, huge profit, sold out for two years; has repeatedly bought the 900 lows and sold into 1,000-1,100. Risk is the memory cycle and future competition.
calls.quote: anytime that it sells off to the lows of 900, I've really enjoyed buying those lows and allowing it to recover

calls.reason: No clear direction and poor risk/reward mid-range; still 34 P/E after a ~26% drop and lagging tech, so not a good investment to him.
calls.quote: I'm not the biggest fan. This would not make sense as a good investment for me

calls.condition: Worst case if broader markets sell off, he expects NBIS to crash hardest.
calls.reason: Calls it a gimmick: $56B market cap on ~$42M profit, huge P/E, pure speculation; irrational stocks fall hardest in selloffs.
calls.quote: I think you're absolutely crazy if you want to invest in in NBIS from the 200 to the 250 range.

calls.condition: Would buy only a small position and be patient; it is testing resistance and could gap down.
calls.reason: 12-year low, 17x earnings, 38% upside to fair value, but revenue no longer growing; cheap can get cheaper.
calls.quote: I wouldn't mind owning maybe a few thousand dollars worth of Nike for them down here

calls.reason: Sarcastically dismisses a viewer's claim that MSTR will rise in 2027, daring them to buy it with a HELOC.
calls.quote: Put a HELOC on your mortgage, and buy MSTR at 155. Would love to see how that ages for you.

notes: Live at 5:25 a.m. Arizona time, five minutes before the 8:30 ET CPI release. Index commentary (QQQ 742-746 range, retesting prior lows) was reactive with no stated bias, so no index call recorded. MSTR bearish view is implied by sarcasm only. NBIS price at call not stated; he refers to a 200-250 range.
